question: A 50-year-old man with a chronic bronchitis who was admitted for a pneumonic episode with a blood culture positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae, with a CMI at penicillin of 0.0125 mg / l. Treatment with 2 million penicillin is started every 4 hours. On the fifth day it continues with a fever of 38ºC. Which of the following decisions do you think is right?

options.opa: I would change the treatment to ceftriaxone because of its greater efficacy.
options.opb: I would add a quinolone to the treatment.
options.opc: I would switch to amoxicillin / clavulanic acid.
options.opd: It would rule out the presence of a pleural empyema.
options.ope: I would continue with the same treatment, assuming that it is simply a problem of time.

CHAIN: "Patient has chronic bronchitis" -> "Admitted for pneumonia" -> "Blood culture positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae" -> "Started on penicillin treatment" -> "Fever persists on day five" -> "Possible inadequate response to penicillin" -> "Adding a quinolone may enhance coverage" -> "Quinolones effective against resistant strains" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient has chronic bronchitis" -> "Admitted for pneumonia" -> "Blood culture positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae" -> "Started on penicillin treatment" -> "Fever persists on day five" -> "Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid may provide better coverage" -> "Not first-line for Streptococcus pneumoniae" -> "Unclear if it would improve outcome" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Patient has chronic bronchitis" -> "Admitted for pneumonia" -> "Blood culture positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae" -> "Started on penicillin treatment" -> "Fever persists on day five" -> "Consider ruling out pleural empyema" -> "Empyema could explain persistent fever" -> "Need imaging to confirm" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Patient has chronic bronchitis" -> "Admitted for pneumonia" -> "Blood culture positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae" -> "Started on penicillin treatment" -> "Fever persists on day five" -> "Assuming treatment failure is premature" -> "Infection may take time to resolve" -> "Continue current treatment" -> 65%
analysis: In this case, the patient has been on penicillin for five days with persistent fever, which raises concerns about treatment failure. Given that the blood culture is positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae and the CMI indicates susceptibility to penicillin, the lack of clinical improvement suggests the possibility of complications such as a pleural empyema. Therefore, ruling out empyema is a critical step before making any changes to the antibiotic regimen. If empyema is present, drainage and possibly a change in antibiotics would be warranted. Thus, the most appropriate decision is to rule out the presence of a pleural empyema.
